text:
Elaine (PM): quick sync — we need a hard cut for the inference-cost control work. can we agree MVP vs v1 scope today?
Marc (Eng): short version: MVP should only have prefix caching + basic batching. advanced quant profiles and dedicated autoscaler are v1.
Vivek (Platform): agree. Dedicated autoscale touches infra and networking; impl estimate 6w. not safe for current ship window.
Sarah (Design): from UX side we can hide advanced toggles behind an "experts" panel for v1. MVP UI: simple on/off caching + suggested batch sizes.
Jordan (CS): customer ask from Atlas and Boreal — they want deterministic latency and a way to opt into dedicated pools. both are okay waiting for v1 if we commit a timeline.
Ryan (Sales): can we promise an ETA? customers pressuring for dedicated capacity by end of Q2. if v1 slips, we lose deal momentum.
Elaine (PM): proposal: ship MVP by 2026-06-15 with: hosted inference, prefix/KV caching, continuous batching, rollout API, basic cost telemetry. v1 by 2026-09-01 with dedicated, autoscale, quant profiles, plus advanced routing.
Marc (Eng): 6w buffer is tight. if we push MVP to mid-June we need to cut a couple more things: per-route cost breakdown and advanced eval hooks are candidates to cut.
Sarah (Design): per-route cost breakdown needs a small panel, but advanced eval hooks require backend work — cut those from MVP.
Jordan (CS): cut is OK if we add a clear communication plan and an interim workaround for per-route visibility (e.g., tagging + csv export).
Vivek (Platform): open blocker: KV cache eviction strategy needs a decision. default LRU is easiest, but not optimal. do we accept LRU for MVP?
Elaine (PM): accept LRU for MVP. add a ticket for heuristic eviction in v1.
Marc (Eng): logging that: "MVP: LRU KV eviction; v1: workload-aware eviction". also flag: model-variant fallback (hot-fallback) — do we want that in MVP?
Ryan (Sales): fallback is critical for some customer SLAs. if we can't do hot-fallback, we should offer a temporary SLA caveat.
Elaine (PM): decision: no hot-fallback in MVP. we'll document a graceful degradation plan and offer an onboarding-runbook for affected customers.
ops-bot: Deploy ticket created: #INF-4721 (mvp-cut: remove advanced-eval-hooks, hide quant toggle).
Marc (Eng): timeline reset note: with cuts we can target +2 weeks saved, so mid-June looks feasible if no new scope creep.
Jordan (CS): I'll draft the customer note and a runbook by EOD Friday.
Sarah (Design): I'll hand off the simplified UI mockups in Figma by tomorrow.
Vivek (Platform): I'll prioritize autoscaler infra spike for the v1 plan.
Elaine (PM): next steps: 1) engineering to update estimates in JIRA by EOD, 2) CS to prepare customer comms, 3) design to deliver mocks, 4) PM will publish an updated milestone doc and freeze scope cuts.
Marc (Eng): quick question — acceptance criteria for MVP: P95 latency under 250ms for 512 tokens on hosted tier, error rate < 0.5% over 24h. ok?
Jordan (CS): Atlas will accept that as a baseline.
Ryan (Sales): want to add a must-have: an opt-in "dedicated preview" for 1 strategic customer if infra spike passes. helps keep deals warm.
Vivek (Platform): we can do a one-customer dedicated preview in a short window but needs a hard guardrail and support rota.
Elaine (PM): noted. I'll add a one-off preview item as a stretch goal, not part of MVP scope.
Marc (Eng): final ask: freeze new feature requests for this initiative until we have MVP metrics for two weeks post-launch.
Elaine (PM): agreed. freeze starts now. I'll post the milestone doc once JIRA is updated.
Jordan (CS): thanks — will align customer expectations accordingly. :thumbsup:
Sarah (Design): ok, moving to mocks.
ops-bot: Reminder set for milestone update review on 2026-04-08 at 10:00 AM.
